summary: Deepest-block separation (block 3 sep_curr_nl, epoch 180; mean +/- sample SD, n = 3): MGC 5.251 +/- 0.050, (c) 5.282 +/- 0.031, (b) 4.879 +/- 0.054, (a) 0.746 +/- 0.012.
P1 PASS: keeping block 0's auxiliary under MGC moves the deepest-block separation by +0.031 +/- 0.022 (c - MGC; 0.6% of the MGC mean), well inside the registered +/-10% band.

P2 FAIL (registered outcome that changes a claim): removing the current-block auxiliary without compensation gives (b) 4.879 +/- 0.054, above the 4.72 threshold. Of the MGC - a gain of 4.504 +/- 0.045, auxiliary removal (b - a) accounts for 4.133 +/- 0.046 (91.7%) and the compensator (MGC - b) for 0.372 +/- 0.013 (8.3%). The compensator's increment is small but has the same sign in every seed (per seed -0.358, -0.374, -0.384 for b - MGC); P2's second clause (every (b) seed below the lowest MGC seed) holds, its first clause does not.
P4 PASS: the SAM-matched cumulative anchor stays low ((a) 0.746 +/- 0.012; SAM-off seed-42 reference 0.7421), so SAM does not drive the D128 separation contrast.

Accuracy contrasts (pooled example-level paired bootstrap, 95% CI, conditional on the checkpoints): S2-TTA c - MGC -0.35 pp [-0.62, -0.08], b - MGC -0.38 pp [-0.64, -0.11], MGC - a +0.24 pp [-0.02, +0.50]; S1 MGC - a -0.29 pp [-0.59, +0.02], b - a -0.43 pp [-0.74, -0.12], c - a -0.42 pp [-0.74, -0.12]. The CIs resample test examples only; the seed-level SD of the paired differences (e.g. S2-TTA c - MGC 0.26, b - MGC 0.26 pp, n = 3) and the hardware mixing are not in them. Arm a ran entirely on Colab A100, arm b entirely on the GB10, so b - a is fully confounded with hardware/software stack.
Prediction churn between two arms at the same seed is 6.69-6.96% of test images at S2-TTA (3-seed means per contrast), below the churn between two seeds of the same arm (8.64-8.83%).

fd_gradient_attenuation.definition: F_d = mean over examples of 1 - min(1, R), R = (1 + e^{beta m}) / (1 + e^{beta (m + gamma P_prev)}), beta = 4, gamma = 0.7; m = current-block goodness margin (true minus wrong label), P_prev = sum of earlier blocks' margins; CI95 = 1.96 sd(ddof=0)/sqrt(N) (published convention; experiments/e3_fd/fd_stats.py)
fd_gradient_attenuation.scope: seed 42 only; first 1024 CIFAR-10 test images; EMA stage1_best weights; CPU. F_d measures the attenuation of the gradient that the cumulative SYMBA term sends to block d's own margin; arm a additionally carries an unattenuated residual-weighted current-block auxiliary, arm b does not.

fd_gradient_attenuation.gradient_fields: grad_mean = mean over examples of beta * sigmoid(-beta (m + gamma P_prev)), the magnitude of the cumulative SYMBA term's gradient w.r.t. block d's own margin; grad_local_mean = the same with gamma = 0 at the same margins (a counterfactual, not a trained gamma = 0 model); their ratio is a mean-level attenuation that weights hard examples (small or negative m) most. Snapshot at the stage1_best EMA weights (Stage-1 epoch 180); it does not describe the training trajectory.
fd_gradient_attenuation.answer: Attenuation is still present in arm b. Seed 42, published wrong labels: F_d(blocks 1-3) = 0.929/0.966/0.971 in arm b (no auxiliary), 0.927/0.954/0.958 in arm a (SAM-matched cumulative with the auxiliary), 0.929/0.950/0.952 in the E3 SAM-off gamma = 0.7 reference; paired b - a at block 3: +0.0138 +/- 0.0075. Arm b's larger F_d follows its larger earlier-block margins (P_prev mean at block 3 12.09 vs 4.75). Its own block-3 margins are also larger (m mean 4.61 vs 0.66), so the gamma = 0 counterfactual gradient is already small: the mean cumulative-term gradient is 0.85 of the counterfactual in arm b vs 0.24 in arm a. The per-example index F_d therefore does not separate the high-separation arm b from the low-separation arm a at this snapshot (n = 1 seed per arm, one checkpoint each).
